title: Retention Statement Balance Computation Sheet — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction
content:
Retention statement balance — computation sheet (Payoff and Loan Satisfaction)

**Issue and good-through date.** A statement is issued within the plan's statement issue period of business days of the request at the plan's statement fee, with the statement date the issue date; every statement other than a retention statement has its good-through date the plan's good-through period of calendar days after its statement date, and a retention statement, the statement on the payoff case of a Borrower Voluntary Payoff requested by the borrower of record on a loan whose maturity case is due and payable, in its extension period or referred to foreclosure, has its good-through date at the statement date plus the statement window days. The statement window days are the plan's good-through period of calendar days, as listed in the plan schedule.

**Balance.** The retention statement balance is the loan's principal balance plus the retention accrual charge plus five statement charges (the statement tax disbursement, the statement hazard disbursement, the statement flood disbursement, the statement servicing fee and the statement maintenance charge), rounded half up to the cent and only at that last step. The five statement charges are each 0.00.

**Retention accrual charge.** The per diem the payoff case carries times the retention accrual days. The retention accrual days are the calendar days from the effective date of the latest posted interest accrual on the loan to the statement date (0 for a loan with no posted interest accrual) plus the statement window days. Interest accruals are those posted on the HECM ledger, or on the Summit loan's ledger for a Summit loan.

| Line | Quantity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | principal balance | the loan record |
| 2 | days since the latest posted interest accrual | the loan's ledger and the statement date |
| 3 | statement window days | the plan's good-through period |
| 4 | retention accrual charge | per diem on the case times the total of lines 2 and 3 |
| 5 | five statement charges | each 0.00 |
| 6 | retention statement balance | lines 1, 4 and 5 added, then rounded half up to the cent |

### Worked example (hypothetical)

A hypothetical case carries a per diem of USD 30.00 on a loan with a principal balance of USD 150000.00, whose latest posted interest accrual is dated 12 days before the statement date; the plan's good-through period is taken from the schedule as 30 days. The retention accrual days are 12 and 30, so 42; the accrual charge is USD 30.00 times 42, USD 1260.00; the retention statement balance is USD 151260.00, good through the 30th calendar day after the statement date. The figures are invented for the illustration.
